candidates.description: User-supplied query parameter `q` is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to `sequelize.query`, allowing arbitrary SQL execution.
candidates.rationale: Line 21 reads `req.query.q` into `criteria`; line 23 interpolates it into a template literal SQL string without parameterization. The only mitigation is a 200-char truncation which does not prevent injection. Verification: send a payload like `' UNION SELECT * FROM Users--` and observe whether user data appears in the JSON response.
candidates.title: SQL injection via unparameterized query in product search

candidates.description: The `email` field from the request body is interpolated directly into a raw SQL SELECT statement, enabling authentication bypass or data exfiltration.
candidates.rationale: Search results confirm line 34 contains `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = ...` with no parameterization. Verification: submit `' OR 1=1--` as email with any password and check if a valid JWT is returned.
candidates.title: SQL injection via email field in login query

candidates.description: The `imageUrl` request body field is passed directly to `fetch()` with no URL scheme, host, or allowlist validation, allowing the server to make arbitrary HTTP requests.
candidates.rationale: Line 19 reads `req.body.imageUrl` into `url`; line 24 calls `fetch(url)` with no validation of protocol, host, or port. The code even acknowledges SSRF via a challenge flag on line 20. Verification: set imageUrl to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` or an internal service and observe whether the response body is written to the uploads directory.
candidates.title: Server-side request forgery via unvalidated imageUrl in profile upload
